_comment: The single source of truth for what RUNTIME_KEY_UNDECLARED treats as a manifest.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The rule was stated in four places -- the code, its comments,
ADR-0010, and the tests -- and drifted between them twice in two days. ADR-0010 was
amended twice; a test had to be reconciled after it contradicted the ADR it cited. Five
rewrites, each fixing one direction and breaking the other, and no single artifact anyone
could point at to answer 'does THIS shape declare?'.
So: this file is the answer. Everything else is generated from it or checked against it.
- core/test/manifest-spec.test.ts runs every case, so the tests ARE the spec
- npm run docs:manifest-spec renders Documentation/MANIFEST_SHAPES.md
- npm run check:manifest-spec fails when the committed doc is not what this produces
- ADR-0010 points here rather than restating the rule
ADDING A SHAPE means adding a row, and the row is simultaneously the test and the
documentation. It cannot be true in one and false in the other.
STATUS, and this is the load-bearing part:
spec        deliberate behaviour. Changing it is a decision and needs an ADR amendment.
known-limit behaviour we know is wrong and have not fixed. The verdict recorded is what
the gate ACTUALLY does today, not what it should do -- so the row is honest
and the suite stays green, while `wanted` records the disagreement.
A spec that recorded only the shapes we got right would be the same drift in a new file.
THE POLICY, from ADR-0010: every false clean this gate produced came from widening the
accept-set to chase a false positive. They are not symmetric -- a rejected manifest is a
visible FAIL an author clears in one edit; an accepted non-manifest is a silent PASS nobody
sees. Ambiguous shapes lose. Four rounds of the opposite policy did not converge.
Every `text` below is a whole document. `expect` is the RUNTIME_KEY_UNDECLARED verdict.
PASS means every key used is declared; FAIL means at least one is not.
